clue.text: Ran into powerful force

definitions.meaning: to run into someone is to encounter them by chance
London's Metropolitan Police, the country's largest police force

explanation.surface: Someone collided with a mighty force, physical or official.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a past-tense verb for encountering someone, and the familiar short name of London's big police force.

clue.text: Trots back?

parts.note: Trots are Trotskyists; a group that backed them within Labour in the 1980s, with a punning hint at a horse's inclination to trot

explanation.walkthrough: 'Trots' looks like horses' gait; here it is slang for Trotskyists. The entryist group that supported them in the Labour Party was this one, and 'tendency' also means an inclination.
explanation.definitionFit: The named faction was a Trotskyist entryist group inside the Labour Party, so it is what backed the Trots.

clue.text: See 1
It's a hot topic in many COBRA negotiations

indicators.note: negotiations treat these words as something to be worked over and rearranged into a new shape

explanation.surface: A burning issue keeps coming up in emergency COBRA committee meetings.
explanation.walkthrough: COBRA is the UK government's crisis committee; here it is just letters for the rearrangement signalled by 'negotiations'.
explanation.definitionFit: The 2015-17 craze for the Labour leader was a much-discussed subject, a talking point of its day.

clue.text: Ditch Conservative leader, uptight and obsessive

indicators.note: the leader of the word Conservative is its opening letter

parts.note: anal, in the Freudian sense, describes someone fussy, uptight and obsessive

explanation.surface: A call to get rid of a fussy, neurotic Tory leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ditch' reads as a verb, get rid of; it is the noun, a dug channel.
explanation.definitionFit: A canal is a man-made waterway, essentially a large ditch carrying water.

clue.text: 15 émigré moving north

indicators.note: moving means the letters of the word émigré are shifted around into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written, accents dropped

explanation.surface: An exile relocating northwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 15 refers to the answer at 15 across, DIET, which is the definition here.
explanation.definitionFit: A diet in the sense of a prescribed eating plan is a regimen, a set programme of food or exercise.

clue.text: Longed for time to take up study

parts.note: a year is a period of time

indicators.note: in a down clue, to take up a word is to lift it so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a den is a private room for study

explanation.surface: Someone who wanted time to pursue their studies.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe having had a strong wish or ache for something, so the past tenses are synonyms.

clue.text: It assesses corrupt statesmen

indicators.note: corrupt says the word statesmen is debased, its letters spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: A vetting process that sees through crooked politicians.
explanation.definitionFit: A means test is an official check of income, used to assess eligibility for state benefits.

clue.text: He's quite right to invest in gas company

indicators.note: to invest in is read literally: the company abbreviation is placed within the gas

parts.note: neon is a noble gas

explanation.surface: Someone deciding to put money into a gas firm, which seems a sensible move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quite right' sounds like approval; it means fairly right-wing.
explanation.definitionFit: A neoconservative is a hawkish American right-winger, a person quite far to the political right.

clue.text: Maggie's heartless, wicked, discriminatory policy

indicators.note: wicked suggests the remaining letters are twisted into a new order
heartless means the central letter of Maggie's is taken out

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: An attack on Margaret Thatcher's cruel, unfair policies.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the middle G of MAGGIES leaves MAGIES, which 'wicked' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Prejudice or unfair treatment on grounds of age is a kind of discrimination, here as a stance or practice.

clue.text: McCluskey, elected a giant of the left

parts.note: Len McCluskey was general secretary of the Unite trade union, a Labour power-broker
to be in is to be elected to office

explanation.surface: The union boss McCluskey, once voted in, became a towering figure on the left.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bolshevik revolutionary leader is one of the most towering figures in socialist history.

clue.text: Am wearing cagoule, shivering; perfect for a dip!

indicators.note: shivering shakes the letters of the preceding words into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone cold in a rain jacket, thinking it is a good moment for a swim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' only joins AM and CAGOULE, the anagram fodder; a cagoule is a lightweight hooded waterproof. 'dip' suggests a swim; it is a sauce for dipping.
explanation.definitionFit: This Mexican avocado mash is served as a dip with tortilla chips.

clue.text: A hero of Hemingway's father?

definitions.meaning: the protagonist of a Hemingway novella, the fisherman Santiago, is known by this title phrase
an informal name for one's dad

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a Hemingway protagonist was based on the writer's own dad.
explanation.definitionFit: Hemingway's novella about Santiago is titled after him; the phrase is also colloquial for a dad.

clue.text: South Beds.? They weren't born here!

parts.note: cots are small beds

explanation.surface: South Bedfordshire residents dismissed as incomers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beds.' poses as the abbreviation for Bedfordshire, an English county; it means cots. The definition jokes that people from Scotland are not natives of England.
explanation.definitionFit: People from north of the border are, from an English viewpoint, incomers rather than natives.

clue.text: Con service sector?

parts.note: the clue word Con is what you get when the letters NOC are given a turn, read backwards

explanation.surface: A query whether the Conservatives form a service industry.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: the answer read as instructions, NOC turned around, gives the clue word Con.
explanation.definitionFit: Matins in the old night office was divided into sections, each of these being one portion of the service.

clue.text: "Man U only won ugly". Not terribly ladylike!

indicators.note: ugly hints at a messy, misshapen version of the words, so their letters are reordered

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for won in sports results tables

explanation.surface: A football fan's grumble that Manchester United only scraped a scrappy win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'won ugly' is football jargon for winning without style; here 'ugly' signals rearranging MAN U, ONLY and W. Man U is Manchester United.
explanation.definitionFit: Behaviour not befitting a lady is lacking in feminine grace, which is what the answer describes.

clue.text: Parliament's strict programme

definitions.meaning: a legislative assembly, as in Japan's or the historic Imperial one

explanation.surface: The legislature has a tough agenda.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a national legislative assembly such as Japan's, and a regulated eating plan.

clue.text: Arousing Labour ire (a bit like Kendall) …

indicators.note: arousing stirs up the letters that follow, mixing them into a new order

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for the Labour Party

explanation.surface: Liz Kendall, the 2015 leadership candidate, stirred some anger within Labour.
explanation.walkthrough: Liz Kendall stood for Labour leader in 2015 as the candidate of the party's centrist, New Labour wing.
explanation.definitionFit: Kendall was the candidate of the New Labour tradition, so she was a follower of the former PM.

clue.text: .. like Flint, having gone for the other extreme?

parts.note: flint is a very hard stone, and Caroline Flint was a Labour MP on the party's right
having gone means having left

explanation.surface: Continuing from 16, an MP like Caroline Flint switching to the opposite wing.
explanation.definitionFit: Opposite the centrist wing of the previous clue lies the radical socialist wing of the party.

clue.text: Quaint time to go

parts.note: to go, informally, is to urinate, to have a wee

explanation.surface: A charmingly old-fashioned moment for leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe something affectedly dainty, cute or old-fashioned in a sentimental way.

clue.text: Held up by Roosevelt, it needed style

indicators.note: Held up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A grand manner that Roosevelt needed and supported.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Held up' does two jobs in a down clue: 'by' places the hidden run within the words, and 'Held up' reads them upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To style someone is to give them a name or title, which is to confer a designation on them.

clue.text: Used by Spooner to let in Tom's visitor?

indicators.note: Spooner, the Oxford don famed for swapping the opening sounds of words, signals that exchange here

parts.note: a flat is a property let out to tenants
a key is what lets you in

explanation.surface: A spoonerised flat key, the thing that gets you in the door.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the opening sounds of FLAT KEY to get CAT FLEA. A tom is a male cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasite that drops in on a tomcat's fur is an uninvited guest of the animal.

clue.text: Batting after tea, English 500 secured

indicators.note: after places the batting element following the tea element

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
a cricket side batting is in
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: A cricket report: batting resumed after the tea break and England reached 500.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fastened with links is held fast, made safe against moving.

clue.text: Save every penny to put money in share issue

indicators.note: in puts the money abbreviation within the share issue

parts.note: scrip is an issue of extra shares to shareholders

explanation.surface: Advice to be thrifty and invest in a share offering.
explanation.definitionFit: To economise severely, being sparing with every coin, is the meaning of this verb.

clue.text: Norman Queen under armour

indicators.note: in a down clue the Queen element sits below the armour element

parts.note: mail is chain armour
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A medieval Norman queen beneath her chain mail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Norman' suggests the Conquest; it is the American novelist Norman Mailer.
explanation.definitionFit: Norman is the first name of the American novelist who wrote The Naked and the Dead.

clue.text: Yawning often, Charles gets married

explanation.surface: Charles marries and is frequently bored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yawning often' reads as describing Charles; it is a gap that is often called yawning.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep gorge or gulf is very commonly described as a yawning one, so this is a cryptic description.

clue.text: Zero emission, green energy backing business on a global scale

indicators.note: backing places the energy element behind the business element

parts.note: trade is business
wind power is green energy with no emissions

explanation.surface: An environmental slogan about clean power supporting global commerce.
explanation.definitionFit: These steady easterly winds form part of the planet-wide circulation of the atmosphere, a weather feature spanning the globe.

clue.text: Woods dumps American model for European one with photogenic face

indicators.note: dumps means one element is discarded and replaced
for says the European letter goes in its place

parts.note: Tiger Woods is the golfer
the Model T was the classic American Ford car

explanation.surface: Tiger Woods swapping an American supermodel girlfriend for a European one.
explanation.definitionFit: The Swiss mountain is famous for its dramatic North Face, much photographed and climbed.

clue.text: Tony Blair's spiritual home, where one drink's well over two thousand pounds?

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a sling is a cocktail, as in Singapore Sling
an imperial ton is 2,240 pounds

explanation.surface: Blair's old London haunt, where a single drink costs a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'pounds' suggest prices, but they are weight. Islington is a north London borough linked with Blair and New Labour.
explanation.definitionFit: The north London borough where Blair lived before 1997 is seen as the home of New Labour metropolitan liberalism.

clue.text: Coal dirt, just like it is up North East?

parts.words: just like it is up North
parts.note: the saying is 'it's grim up north', about the north of England

explanation.surface: Coal dust, typical of how bleak things are in northern England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's grim up North' is a British saying about the industrial north of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Grime is soot and ingrained filth, the kind of muck coal leaves behind.

clue.text: Revolting peasant mingling with procession — could it be Jeremy?

indicators.note: mingling with mixes the two named elements together into a new order

parts.note: Wat Tyler led the Peasants' Revolt of 1381
a parade is a procession

explanation.surface: A rebellious peasant joining a march, possibly Jeremy Corbyn himself.
explanation.walkthrough: An indirect anagram: TYLER and PARADE are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeremy Corbyn headed Labour, so he is an example of the head of a political organisation.

clue.text: Worry at constituency leader going missing

indicators.note: leader going missing means the opening letter is removed

parts.note: a seat is a parliamentary constituency

explanation.surface: Anxiety that the local constituency's head has vanished.
explanation.definitionFit: As in 'what's bothering you?', this verb means to trouble or nag at someone.
